content.rendered:
God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind. Fear is not from the Father. Power, love, and a sound mind are. The believer facing anything today is walking in the wrong spirit if fear is leading the conversation.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, August 6, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.”
2 Timothy 1:7 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Paul writes 2 Timothy from a Roman prison, near the end of his life. He is pouring the last of his energy into strengthening his spiritual son Timothy, a young pastor facing a difficult ministry season. In chapter one, he tells Timothy to stir up the gift of God that is in him. And then, in verse seven, he gives one of the sharpest diagnostic sentences in the whole New Testament. If fear is dominating, that spirit is not from God.

The Amplified Bible Classic Edition opens up the depth of what Paul is saying: “For God did not give us a spirit of timidity (of cowardice, of craven and cringing and fawning fear), but [He has given us a spirit] of power and of love and of calm and well-balanced mind and discipline and self-control” (2 Timothy 1:7 AMPC). Cowardice. Craven. Cringing. The negative shadow is drawn sharply. And what has been given instead is power, love, calm, discipline, self-control.

The Passion Translation puts it this way: “For God will never give you the spirit of fear, but the Holy Spirit who gives you mighty power, love, and self-control” (2 Timothy 1:7 TPT). Never. God will never give you the spirit of fear. If fear is what you are carrying, you did not get it from Him.

This is diagnostic. When the believer feels themselves gripped by an oppressive, controlling, life-shrinking fear, the first thing to recognise is the source. The fear is not from God. Once the source is identified, the counterfeit spirit can be refused in the name of Jesus. In its place, the believer receives what God has actually given. Power. Love. A sound mind.

Power, in Greek, is dunamis, the same word we saw in Ephesians 1:19-20 of the resurrection strength operating in the believer. Love, agapē, the settled decision to seek the good of the other, which drives out the enemy’s tactics of division. A sound mind, sōphronismos, means self-controlled, disciplined thinking, the mind that has not been hijacked by anxiety. Together, these three form the internal atmosphere of the Spirit-filled believer. And they are what God has actually given. Not fear. Never fear. Something else entirely.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the practical application today is worth writing down. Whenever fear tries to lead the conversation in your mind, name it out loud in the name of Jesus. This spirit of fear is not from God. And then receive out loud what He has actually given. I have the Spirit of power. I have the Spirit of love. I have the Spirit of a sound mind. Repeat until the internal atmosphere shifts. It will shift. The believer’s authority over fear is a daily practice, and 2 Timothy 1:7 is the anchor Scripture for that practice.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have not given me a spirit of fear. Fear is not from You. In the name of Jesus, I refuse the spirit of fear that has tried to lead the conversation in my mind. I receive what You have actually given. I receive the Spirit of power. I receive the Spirit of love. I receive the Spirit of a sound mind. My inner atmosphere is aligned with the Spirit You have placed within me. I walk in that atmosphere today, confident, love-filled, and clear-headed. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

God has not given me a spirit of fear. He has given me power, love, and a sound mind. I refuse fear in the name of Jesus and receive what my Father has actually given.

Go Deeper in the Word

  • 2 Timothy 1:6-8 (NKJV): Stir up the gift of God within you
  • Romans 8:15 (NKJV): You have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear
  • 1 John 4:18 (NKJV): Perfect love casts out fear
